AAI Limited t/as AAMI v Ul Hassan [2025] NSWPIC 616; 
 (19 November 2025)

system:
You are coding NSW motor accident decisions for a research dataset. Read the decision text supplied and assign each ordinal score from the text alone.

Score each dimension INDEPENDENTLY. A decision describing a severe case will score high on some dimensions and not others: severe physical injury does not by itself imply a contested proceeding, a disputed liability, or a prominent psychological component. Judge each scale against its own definition and resist letting an overall impression of severity carry across the scales.

If the text does not support a judgement on a dimension, give the lowest score rather than guessing upward, and say so in `uncertain`.

DECISION TEXT:
--- Catchwords ---
MOTOR ACCIDENTS -

Motor Accident Injuries Act 2017 ; settlement approval pursuant to section 6.23 ; self-represented claimant suffered orthopaedic injuries including left second-fifth rib fractures, right scaphoid and trapezius fracture, and a small undisplaced fracture of the anterior distal tibia; claimant made a good recovery but continued to suffer symptoms and incapacity and disability which impacted his capacity to earn; claimant declined to undergo independent whole person impairment assessment; Held – past economic loss and future economic loss in a proposed settlement was approved; insurer to have credit in respect to statutory payments made to or on behalf of the claimant.

--- Key Paragraphs ---
[para 26] Addresses WPI assessment issue and claimant’s refusal of independent assessment.
26. I indicated that I had some concerns about the WPI assessment. The insurer's representative, Mr Izzard indicated that the insurer had offered the claimant the opportunity of an independent WPI assessment but he had declined. I reminded the claimant that an independent assessment could be arranged but he was adamant that he wanted the matter finalised and that he would not attend any further medical examinations.

[para 28] States non-economic loss entitlement position which affects damages heads.
28. The insurer submitted correctly that the claimant was not entitled to damages for

non-economic loss.

[para 29] Sets pre-injury weekly earnings and period to return to work; anchors past loss.
29. The claimant's net weekly earnings at the time of the accident were $955.76 per week. It was noted that he was cleared to return to pre-accident work from 11 November 2024, that is, 62 weeks after the accident. The buffer allowed included refundable tax payments made by AAMI of $9,639.00. I consider that the allowance for past economic loss is appropriate.

[para 33] Applies s 4.7 MAI Act assumptions and competing earning capacity figures.
33. As to the assumptions that need to be made pursuant to s 4.7 of the MAI Act it was assumed by the insurer that, but for the motor accident, the claimant would have obtained employment in the construction industry earning between $80,000 to $100,000 per annum or $1,538.46 to $1,923.08 gross per week although the claimant's ability to maintain employment in the construction industry was effectively untested prior to the motor accident. The insurer referred to an opinion expressed by Ms Ciara Lynch, rehabilitation counsellor who opined that the claimant had considerable retained earning capacity including roles as a delivery driver, where he could earn $907.70 per week, ICT Support Technician earning $1,482 gross per week or a customer service representative earning $1,499 gross per week.

[para 34] Identifies the 350,000 future economic loss buffer proposed by the insurer.
34. The insurer allowed a buffer of $350,000 including an allowance for future economic loss, which it considered was appropriate.

[para 38] Member’s reasoning approving past and future economic loss buffers.
38. I confirm that the allowance of $70,000 for past economic loss is appropriate. In considering the amount allowed for future economic loss I consider that the submissions made by the insurer are appropriate and that the buffer of $350,000 is in the appropriate range in all the circumstances.

[para 39] Express finding that the total settlement is just, fair and reasonable.
39. I am satisfied that the total proposed settlement of $420,000 is just, fair and reasonable and within the range of likely potential damages assessments for the claim were the matter to be assessed by the Commission, taking into account the nature and extent of the claim and the injuries, disabilities, impairments and losses sustained by the claimant.

[para 41] Order allowing insurer credit for statutory benefits; final approval.
41. Having considered all the material available, I am satisfied that the proposed settlement should be approved. I note that the insurer is entitled to deduct the sum of $61,950.47 in respect of statutory benefits paid to or on behalf of the claimant.

Assign each score:
  Injury Burden Intensity (0-4): overall physical burden of the injuries: 0 minimal, 4 catastrophic/multiple major injuries
  Treatment Burden (0-3): extent of treatment, surgery and ongoing care: 0 none or minimal, 3 extensive surgery and long-term care
  Work Impact Severity (0-3): loss of working capacity: 0 none, 3 total incapacity
  Legal Procedural Complexity (0-3): procedural complexity of the proceeding: 0 straightforward, 3 heavily contested
  Psychological Injury Emphasis (0-2): weight the decision gives to psychological injury: 0 none, 2 central
  Liability Clarity (0-2): how clear fault is: 0 seriously disputed, 2 clear or admitted
  Causation Complexity (0-2): difficulty attributing the condition to the accident: 0 straightforward, 2 heavily contested
  Pre-existing Condition Salience (0-2): how prominent a prior condition is in the decision: 0 absent, 2 central
